urn:eigenius:core:description: A typed optimisation-problem statement consumable by a JuMP-backed institution. v1 carries the model definition as Julia source in `model_source`: a function `build_model(optimizer)` that returns a `JuMP.Model` with all variables / constraints / objective set. The institution evaluates the source against its solver factory at dispatch time. Decision-variable names declared in `variables_declared` are used to extract the primal solution as a name → value map.
Julia source defining a `build_model(optimizer)` function returning a `JuMP.Model`. The institution worker evaluates this source in a scope where `JuMP` and the solver package are imported.
Names of the decision variables exposed as solution keys. These are the symbol names attached to JuMP `VariableRef`s that the institution surfaces as the primal solution map.

The three orthogonal status fields a JuMP solve returns (D27 §4.2 verified note). Stringified MOI enum names — `OPTIMAL`, `INFEASIBLE`, `LOCALLY_SOLVED`, `TIME_LIMIT`, `FEASIBLE_POINT`, `INFEASIBILITY_CERTIFICATE`, `NO_SOLUTION`, etc. The institution does not re-encode these as Eigon enums; the MOI vocabulary IS the contract.
MOI termination status, stringified (e.g. `"OPTIMAL"`, `"INFEASIBLE"`, `"DUAL_INFEASIBLE"`, `"LOCALLY_SOLVED"`, `"TIME_LIMIT"`).
MOI primal-solution status, stringified (`"FEASIBLE_POINT"`, `"INFEASIBILITY_CERTIFICATE"`, `"NO_SOLUTION"`, etc.).
MOI dual-solution status, stringified.

Claims an optimisation outcome for `problem`: an objective value, a primal solution as a name → value map, optionally a dual solution, and the MOI status block. The 'certificate' is the (primal_solution, dual_solution, status_block) triple — JuMP has no atomic certificate object. AutoOnLoad re-checks primal feasibility + (for LP) the duality gap; for NLPs it re-runs and confirms `LOCALLY_SOLVED` agreement (subject to local-optimum non-determinism).
The OptimisationProblem this outcome is about.
The optimal objective value (`JuMP.objective_value(m)`).
Primal solution as a JSON map from declared variable name to numeric value (`JuMP.value(var)`).
Dual solution as a JSON map from constraint name to dual value (`JuMP.dual(constraint)`). LP / convex QP only.
Embedded StatusBlock recording the three MOI status fields.

Claims `problem` is infeasible, with an institution-validatable witness. AutoOnLoad replays the witness: for `farkas_dual`, the institution checks the linear-algebra Farkas conditions; for `iis`, it re-solves the IIS subset and confirms it remains infeasible. NB: HiGHS supports Farkas duals but not IIS — IIS-witness Infeasible resources committed against the HiGHS institution return Verdict::Undecidable. Solver-specific capability is recorded on each per-solver Institution.
Discriminator for the infeasibility witness shape: `"farkas_dual"` (a dual ray; uniform across LP solvers when supported) or `"iis"` (an irreducible infeasible subset; solver-specific).
Opaque JSON witness payload, interpreted by the institution per `witness_kind`. For `farkas_dual`: a constraint-name → multiplier map. For `iis`: a list of constraint names that form the IIS.

Claims a primal-feasible bound and a best dual / objective-bound for `problem` short of optimality (e.g. from a time-capped MIP solve). `lower` / `upper` are the best-known objective-bound and incumbent-value (orientation depends on sense). AutoOnLoad re-runs with the same time limit and confirms the achieved bounds are at least as good. Class name is intentionally distinct from `julia:intervals:BoundedBy` — different fibre, different IRI, no overlap.
Lower bound on the objective value (best-known dual bound for a Max problem; best-known incumbent for Min).
Upper bound on the objective value (best-known incumbent for Max; best-known dual bound for Min).

OnDemand input class for qc_bounds_after: a problem and a time limit (seconds). The institution time-caps the solve via `set_time_limit_sec(m, s)` and returns the best bounds the solver had at the cap.
Solver wall-clock time limit in seconds.

OnDemand result class for qc_sensitivity_analysis (LP only). Two JSON maps: `objective_ranges_kv` mapping variable name → [d_lo, d_hi] objective-coefficient ranges, and `rhs_ranges_kv` mapping constraint name → [d_lo, d_hi] RHS ranges. From `JuMP.lp_sensitivity_report` (solver-agnostic — works wherever the solver exposes basis status).
Map from variable name to [d_lo, d_hi] objective-coefficient sensitivity range.
Map from constraint name to [d_lo, d_hi] RHS sensitivity range.
